home.description: Posters of generative shader art. Shape each one with four controls, choose its colours, and order the version you made.
home.headline: Art made by code. Tuned by you.
home.lede: Every ShaderPaper poster is a shader: a small program that paints the image. Pick one, shape it with four controls, choose its colours, and order the version you made.
home.collectionsTitle: Six ways of drawing with code
home.howTitle: The poster you order is the one you made
home.howBody: On each poster's page the shader itself runs in your browser, so every change is drawn as you make it.
home.step1Body: Each poster is its own shader, in six collections from geometric tilings to 3D materials.
home.step2Body: Up to four controls change what the shader draws. A new variation gives you a different composition.
home.step3Body: Choose a palette and how strong the colours are: natural, balanced or vivid.
home.step4Body: Pick a size and a frame on the poster's page; every price is shown there.
home.printTitle: Rendered from your design, printed to order
home.printBody: Your design (the poster, its variation, its controls and colours) is saved with your order, and the print file is rendered from it by the same shader you saw.
home.tbwPrint: The print partner, paper stock, production time and delivery times.

about.title: About
about.lede: ShaderPaper sells posters of generative art that you shape before you order.
about.what1: Each poster is a shader: a short program that computes the colour of every point of the image. The same program can draw many images; the variation number and up to four controls decide which one.
about.what2: On a poster's page the shader runs in your browser, so the preview changes as you move the controls. Your design is saved with the order, and the print file is rendered from it.
about.catalogue: The catalogue has {n} posters in {c} collections.

about.print1: Posters are made to order: a poster is printed after someone orders it.

faq.lede: Short answers about the posters and the customiser. Where the answer is not decided yet, the page says so.

q.preview: Will the print look like the preview?
q.sizes: Which sizes and frames are there?
q.paper: What paper is it printed on?

a.shader: A small program, usually run on a graphics card, that computes the colour of each pixel. Every ShaderPaper poster is one.
a.customise: Each poster has up to four shape controls, a choice of palettes and a colour strength (natural, balanced or vivid). You can also ask for a new variation: another composition of the same shader.
a.variation: A number that seeds the shader. Variation 1 is the image in the catalogue; other numbers give other compositions. Your variation and settings are saved with your order and in the page address, so you can share them.
a.preview: The print file is rendered by the same shader with your settings. Colours on paper and on a screen never match exactly.
a.sizes: Each poster's page lists its sizes and frames with their prices.
a.account: No. You can check out as a guest; an account keeps your orders and addresses.
